# Recorded dialogue

The existing stairwell, archive and intercom performances are human voice recordings edited for LAST LIGHT. The new chapter guidance and combat warning use a separately credited synthetic voice. English speech has matching English and Chinese subtitles. Editors trimmed the source takes, filtered room rumble, added fades and encoded mono AAC for playback in the game.

- BlueSiren. Three excerpts used for `lost.m4a`, `calling.m4a` and `trapped.m4a`. [Female voice sample: Talking, Fighting noises](https://freesound.org/people/BlueSiren/sounds/379301/).
- pyro13djt. One urgent evacuation take used for `evacuate.m4a`. [Get Out Of Here.wav](https://freesound.org/people/pyro13djt/sounds/331909/).

Both creators released their recordings under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).

The lift, personnel terminal, switchboard and roof circuit use six edits of the unprocessed voice session performed by RICHERlandTV. The clips are `gap`, `doors`, `register`, `exchange`, `circuit` and `farewell`. LAST LIGHT selected phrases, edited pauses, combined takes for the terminal and roof, equalized, normalized and encoded them. The public-address and archive timbres are shaped by equalization during playback. These edited announcements are licensed under CC BY 4.0. [Things A Machine Might Say by RICHERlandTV](https://freesound.org/people/RICHERlandTV/sounds/705751/) · [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

The reply behind Gary’s door uses HorathDrak’s recording `thank you.ogg`. The restored evacuation tape uses a single, trimmed take from GreasyPlastic’s voice session. Both were edited, equalized and encoded for the game. [HorathDrak’s recording](https://freesound.org/people/HorathDrak/sounds/449166/) · [GreasyPlastic’s performance](https://freesound.org/people/GreasyPlastic/sounds/790133/) · [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)

## Synthetic chapter guidance

The localized boiler, gramophone, rooftop and gaze warning lines are original fictional dialogue rendered offline with [Kokoro-82M v1.0](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M) using its Apache-2.0 licensed weights. The English and Mandarin takes use the stock `af_heart` and `zf_xiaobei` voices, respectively. These tracks use edited pauses, light equalization and loudness control. They do not represent the creator's voice. The two editions share the same office and rooftop lines and use their own boiler instructions.
